consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué es verdad sobre quien habla.

items.audio: When I first moved here, the traffic kept me awake every night. Now I hardly notice it, but my sister, who is staying with me, can't sleep at all. She says she could never live with it.
opciones: The traffic no longer troubles the speaker.
The speaker still cannot sleep because of the traffic.
The speaker's sister has got used to the noise.

feedback.es: Al principio el ruido le quitaba el sueño, pero ahora casi no lo nota; quien no duerme es su hermana, no quien habla.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige cómo llegaron finalmente a la costa.

items.audio: We were going to drive to the coast, but the car broke down. A neighbour offered us his van, although it was too small for everyone. In the end, we took the train.
opciones: They all went in a neighbour's van.
They repaired the car and left later.

feedback.es: Iban a ir en auto, el vecino ofreció una camioneta demasiado pequeña y al final tomaron el tren: usaron transporte público.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué siente la persona sobre su decisión.

items.audio: If I had accepted the job in Madrid, I would be living there now. Sometimes I wonder about it. But if I had gone, I wouldn't have met my partner, so I have no regrets.
opciones: The speaker is content with the decision.
The speaker wishes to have moved to Madrid.
The speaker plans to move to Madrid soon.

feedback.es: Duda a veces, pero concluye que no se arrepiente: si hubiera aceptado el trabajo, no habría conocido a su pareja.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige cuál es la postura de la portavoz.

items.audio: The spokesperson admitted that the company had made a mistake, but insisted that nobody had been hurt. She promised to publish a full report, although critics claim the figures are exaggerated.
opciones: She denies that the company did anything wrong at all.
She admits some blame but denies any harm.
She refuses to give any more information to critics.

feedback.es: Admite un error pero insiste en que nadie salió herido: acepta parte de la culpa y niega el daño.

consigna.es: Lee el mensaje y elige qué opina la autora de lo que dice su compañera.

items.texto: Hi Lena, it's been ages! I've been living in Leeds since September and I still can't get used to the weather. Back home it never snowed, so I wasn't used to wearing three coats! Lately I've been cooking a lot because the food at the café is so expensive. My flatmate says I'll get used to it, but I'm not so sure. Honestly, I miss the sun. Write soon!
opciones: She believes her flatmate is probably right.
She is planning to leave Leeds soon.
She doubts what her flatmate says.

feedback.es: Su compañera dice que se acostumbrará, pero ella responde «I'm not so sure» y añade que extraña el sol: no está convencida.

consigna.es: Lee el correo y elige para qué lo escribe el cliente.

items.texto: Dear Mr Hill, On Monday I took my car to your garage because the brakes were making a strange noise. You promised to have it ready by Wednesday, but I only got it back on Friday, and the noise is still there. I'm not asking for a refund, but I would like your mechanic to look at it again, free of charge. I hope we can sort this out.
opciones: To ask the garage to look at the brakes again at no cost
To ask for a refund for the repair
To thank the garage for returning the car by Wednesday

feedback.es: Pide que revisen de nuevo el auto sin costo; aclara que no quiere un reembolso, y se queja de que el ruido sigue.

consigna.es: Lee el texto y elige cómo se siente la autora al final.

items.texto: Last Friday I found a wallet with two hundred dollars inside. Money is a problem this month, and I could easily have kept it. But the owner's address was on his card, so I took the wallet to his door. He was so grateful that he insisted on buying me lunch. I'm glad I did the right thing. Still, I sometimes think about the laptop I could have bought.
opciones: She wishes she had kept the money.
She is satisfied, though not free from regret.
She is angry that the owner did not thank her.

feedback.es: Se alegra de haber hecho lo correcto, pero aún piensa en la laptop que pudo comprar: satisfacción con un pequeño pesar.

consigna.es: Lee el artículo y elige qué opina el autor del titular de un informe.

items.texto: A new study claims that teenagers who sleep less than six hours tend to get lower marks. The researchers, however, admit that their sample was small, and other things, such as diet or stress, may well be involved. Nevertheless, the headline in one report states that lack of sleep causes bad results, which is arguably exaggerated.
opciones: They describe the study's results fairly.
They say more than the study can really show.
They are too cautious about what the study found.

feedback.es: El autor dice que el titular es «arguably exaggerated»: afirma una causa que el estudio no puede demostrar.

consigna.es: Elige la forma que completa la frase.

items.texto: Night shifts are still hard for me, but I ___ sleeping in the daytime more and more.

feedback.es: «More and more» indica un proceso en curso: am getting used to + -ing. «Am used to» ya sería costumbre y «used to» no lleva -ing.

items.texto: My teacher made me ___ the whole essay again because of one small mistake.

feedback.es: Después de make + persona va el verbo sin to: made me write. Con get sí se usa to (got me to write).

consigna.es: Elige el verbo que completa la condición.

items.texto: Tom missed the last train last night. If he had caught it, he ___ at home now.

feedback.es: La condición es pasada, pero el resultado es de hoy (now): condicional mixto, had + participio en el if y would + verbo en la otra parte.

consigna.es: Elige el conector que completa la frase.

items.texto: You can borrow my laptop ___ you promise to look after it.

feedback.es: Provided that introduce una condición necesaria: te la presto si prometes cuidarla. Unless significaría lo contrario.

consigna.es: Elige la expresión que encaja en la frase.

items.texto: Mia ran up all the stairs, so she arrived ___.

feedback.es: Out of breath es quedarse sin aliento por el esfuerzo; out of order es «averiado» y out of date, «desactualizado».

consigna.es: Elige el verbo compuesto que completa la frase.

items.texto: After their argument, Jo and Mia didn't speak for weeks, but last night they finally ___.

feedback.es: Make up es reconciliarse después de una pelea; fall out es pelearse y hit it off, llevarse bien desde el principio.

consigna.es: Elige la expresión que completa el mensaje.

items.texto: It's a surprise party for Clara, so please don't ___ before Saturday!

feedback.es: Spill the beans es revelar un secreto sin querer; break the ice rompe el hielo y bite the bullet es aguantar algo difícil.

consigna.es: Elige el adjetivo que describe ese artículo.

items.texto: The article gives only one side and ignores the critics, so it is clearly ___.

feedback.es: Biased es parcial: favorece a un solo lado. Balanced y accurate describirían un artículo que muestra ambas posturas o es exacto.

consigna.es: Explica por qué llegaste agotado anoche: llevabas varias horas haciendo algo.

items.respuesta: I was exhausted last night because I had been working in the garden for five hours.
aceptadas: When I got home I was out of breath, because I had been running for an hour and I had not eaten.

feedback.es: Had been + -ing cuenta la actividad que duraba antes de llegar agotado; for + duración indica cuánto, y because explica la causa.

consigna.es: Di cómo sería tu vida hoy si hubieras estudiado otra carrera y por qué no lo hiciste.

items.respuesta: If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now. However, I chose design because I have always loved drawing.
aceptadas: If I'd studied law, I would be living in another city now. I didn't choose it since I wanted to stay near my family.

feedback.es: Condicional mixto: if I had + participio para la decisión pasada y would be o would + verbo para el efecto actual; explica la razón con because.

notes: P1 corregidos: gramatica.2 (get+to demasiado fácil y con el audio de escucha.2 delatando la clave) -> make + verbo sin to; gramatica.3 (hueco en el if, igual que el tercer condicional de N4, y calcado del audio escucha.3) -> hueco en la oración principal del condicional mixto; gramatica.4 (consequently ~ as a result de N4) -> provided that frente a unless; gramatica.1 -> am getting used to frente a am used to (proceso vs costumbre).

P1 corregidos de clave: lectura.2 (la correcta era la única que repetía palabras del texto), lectura.1 (la correcta repetía 'getting used to'), lectura.4 (una opción también era defendible), lectura.3 (texto sin apoyo explícito para 'orgullo'); vocabulario.4 repetía 'claim' de lectura.4 y escucha.4.

Discriminación: escucha.1 exige seguir a dos personas (quien habla vs su hermana), escucha.2 sustituye el tema de reparaciones de N4 por un relato con plan cambiado y tres medios de transporte; vocabulario.1-4 pasan a out of breath, made up, spill the beans, biased; escritura.1 pide had been + duración, escritura.2 cambia de escenario para no copiar el audio escucha.3.
Rúbricas: se añaden variantes por la expansión de I'd a 'I would' de la app (would been, if i would) y más duraciones y conectores de causa.
P2 residual: escucha.2 es el ítem de escucha más fácil del banco; cubre principio a fin del nivel (clases 7-86).
